submissions.explanation:
Assuming the imported theorem `OAI.PiExponent.main`, the campaign's shared definition satisfies

$$\operatorname{PiIrrationality.UpperBound}(2).$$

The argument uses only the theorem's first conjunct: for every real exponent $\nu>2$, a single integer threshold $Q\ge2$ makes $q^{-\nu}\le|\pi-p/q|$ hold for all integer numerators $p$ and integer denominators $q\ge Q$. Choosing an exponent strictly between $2$ and $2+\varepsilon$ supplies the strict inequality required by the campaign.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and apply this assertion with $\nu=2+\varepsilon/2$. Let $Q\ge2$ be the resulting threshold. Since $Q$ is nonnegative, its natural-number counterpart `Q.toNat` has the same integer value. Every natural denominator above this threshold satisfies $q\ge2$, so its real value is greater than $1$.

Real powers with a base greater than $1$ are strictly increasing in their exponent. Therefore every such $q$ and every integer $p$ satisfy

$$\frac{1}{q^{2+\varepsilon}}=q^{-(2+\varepsilon)}<q^{-(2+\varepsilon/2)}\le\left|\pi-\frac pq\right|.$$

The threshold is uniform in $p$ and $q$, exactly as required by `PiIrrationality.UpperBound 2`. The supremum conjunct of the OpenAI theorem is unused.

This submission is a reduction to `OAI.PiExponent.main`, which is currently an open theorem on Prove2me. The reduction verifies the implication; the campaign goal remains conditional on a verified proof of that dependency.
